analysis:
The PR changes only documentation: docs/developer/build.md (CI Runner Routing section, head lines 239-262) and docs/developer/test.md (shard routing note near line 99 and routing-check description near line 1371). It documents that each provider test shard reads its own routing lane (test-provider-K, via format('test-provider-{0}', matrix.shard)) and that the sandbox plane grants a lane whole or not at all. No source, workflow, protocol, key handling, attestation or authorization code is modified in the supplied evidence.

Threat-model relevance is limited. The routing text concerns read-only CI job placement (Darkbloom Sandbox vs Blacksmith fallback). It does not touch the provider trust boundaries TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-010, TB-011, TB-012 or TB-013, and none of A-001 to A-019 is affected. The unchanged build.md text keeps the existing controls: routing off by default, fork PRs keep the fallback, a grant is used only when exact labels match, and errors keep the fallback. Release, signing, publication and model registration keep literal Blacksmith labels. The documentation does not weaken those statements.

Remaining integration question: the actual workflow files (.github/workflows/ci.yml, darkbloom-route.yml) and the routing tests were not supplied. I therefore cannot verify that the documented per-shard lanes match the implementation, or that release/signing jobs still avoid the sandbox runners. That is a documentation-accuracy and coverage limit, not evidence of a regression. If the workflow change ships in the same PR, a reviewer should confirm that signing and publication lanes are not routed to sandboxes, and that the lane name is not attacker-controlled from PR content.
